items.topic: BaseClient design for HTTP client variants
items.context: Codebase analysis reveals the 5 clients are not uniform. AuditorClient has doJSONAccept (accepting multiple HTTP status codes), BrowserAutomationClient has doRaw (fetching binary data with content-type), and AgentManagerClient caches its resolved URL with a mutex. The embedded BaseClient struct from round 1 decision d1 needs to accommodate these variants without becoming over-engineered.

options.label: BaseClient covers doGet/doJSON/resolveBaseURL/parseError only; variants stay on child
options.rationale: BaseClient handles the common 80% (doGet, doJSON, resolveBaseURL, parseError with configurable service name). doJSONAccept stays on AuditorClient as a thin wrapper calling BaseClient internals. doRaw stays on BrowserAutomationClient. AgentManagerClient overrides resolveBaseURL to add caching. Keeps the base simple and avoids premature generalization.

options.label: BaseClient covers all variants with configurable options
options.rationale: Add acceptStatuses param to doJSON, a doRaw method, and optional caching to resolveBaseURL. Maximizes deduplication but makes the base type more complex and couples unrelated concerns.

items.topic: Scope of long_files to address (43 violations)
items.context: The plan currently lists only 6 files, but the codebase has 43 long_files violations. The top offenders not in the plan include: main.go (1363 lines), review_handler_test.go (1355 lines), git_runner.go (1149 lines), git_runner_fake_test.go (997 lines), diff_service_test.go (794 lines), agent_manager_client_test.go (779 lines), diff_service.go (763 lines), visual_capture_storage.go (649 lines), and many more. Hitting long_files <10 requires addressing most of these. The HTTP client dedup and test refactoring will reduce counts in some files, but the largest files are unrelated to those patterns.

options.label: Address all files exceeding the threshold via splitting/extracting
options.rationale: To hit long_files <10, we need to bring most of the 43 violating files under threshold. This means splitting large service files, test files, and handlers. Comprehensive but significantly more work than initially scoped.

options.label: Only address files touched by HTTP client and test refactoring phases
options.rationale: Rely on deduplication to reduce counts in files we're already touching. Accept that we may not hit the <10 target for long_files but will improve the score significantly. Lower effort, lower risk.

items.topic: ScenarioReviewPanel TODO: is the unified review endpoint stable?
items.context: Round 1 decision d4 chose to implement TODO functionality and remove markers. The App.tsx TODO (scroll-to-line) is straightforward UI work. However, the ScenarioReviewPanel.tsx TODO says: 'Remove this client-side fallback once the unified review endpoint is stable. The server-side calculation (review_readiness.go) is authoritative and also includes standards/blocking-violations checks that this fallback cannot replicate.' Removing this fallback prematurely could break review readiness display if the endpoint isn't fully stable.

options.label: Verify endpoint stability first, then remove fallback
options.rationale: Check that the unified review endpoint in review_readiness.go covers all cases the fallback handles. If confirmed stable, remove the fallback. If not, convert the TODO to a tracked issue and just remove the comment. This is safest and aligns with the TODO's own guidance.

options.label: Just remove the TODO comments, don't implement either TODO
options.rationale: The goal is tech_debt_markers=0. Simply removing the TODO comments achieves that metric without the risk of UI changes. File separate items for the actual work. Fastest path to the target.

items.topic: What line count threshold defines a 'long file'?
items.context: The tidiness-manager reports 43 long_files but the plan doesn't specify what threshold triggers that violation. Knowing the threshold is critical for determining which files need splitting and how aggressively. The 5th-largest file is diff_service_test.go at 794 lines; the 43rd-largest file might be as small as 100-150 lines. The refactoring strategy depends heavily on where the line is drawn.

options.label: Run tidiness-manager to get the exact threshold and full violation list
options.rationale: Before planning splits, we need the actual data. Run `tidiness-manager recommend-refactors git-control-tower --limit 50 --format json` during execution to get the precise list. The plan should instruct the executor to do this as step 0. Recommended because we shouldn't plan file splits without knowing which files are actually flagged.

options.label: Assume 150 lines threshold based on plan's 'no new files exceed 150 lines' rule
options.rationale: The plan already says no new files should exceed 150 lines. Use that as the working threshold. May not match tidiness-manager's actual threshold.

items.text: The codebase is significantly larger than the top-5 list in the description suggests. There are 151 Go files totaling 32,346 lines. The top 20 files alone account for ~12,500 lines. main.go (1,363 lines), review_handler_test.go (1,355 lines), and git_runner.go (1,149 lines) are the largest but weren't mentioned in the original description. The HTTP client dedup will help (5 clients total ~1,117 lines) but won't address the bulk of the long_files count.

plan_updates: Identified gaps in BaseClient variant handling, scope of long_files violations beyond the original top-5 list, and risk around the ScenarioReviewPanel TODO stability. Plan needs to expand Phase 1 to specify variant handling, Phase 2 to cover the full list of violating test files, and Phase 4 to gate the fallback removal on endpoint stability verification.
